# Background

See [my 2024 medium article](https://medium.com/@barrymann2/introducing-an-aep-data-dictionary-e760e8ad38e1#). Following feedback and suggestions, I have rewritten these instructions to make it easier for suers to produce an AEP Data Health Dashboard for themselves.

# Business Benefits

- Enables easy governance
  - Spotting data errors
  - Allowing understanding of data collection to a non technical audience, eg:
    - Are we collecting Currency Codes?
    - Are we collecting event data for the full ecommerce funnel?
    - Does the data contain formatting errors eg camelCase errors?
    - Erroneous whitespace?
    - What do the volumes look like?
    - What are the top 5 values for each field
    - Is new data coming through to AEP eg carousel clicks?
- Bad examples for the Launch team to fix.
- Allows data collection teams to hand it over to the orchestration teams

# This Demo Uses Luma Web Test Data

To protect client confidentiality, this demo was built using Adobe's Luma test dataset—a publicly available sample dataset that mimics retail web data. You can run everything as shown using Luma data.

When that is stood up, , simply replace the input folder contents with your own exported client data, re-run the tool, and generate a custom data dictionary for **your** organisation!

# How It Works

The AEP Health Dashboard is designed to process .ndjson files exported from Adobe Experience Platform (AEP) via either FTP or Azure Blob Storage. It expects to find daily, incremental .zip files containing .ndjson exports from your AEP dataset.

This tool does **not** use any APIs. It is a rudimentary vibe coded prototype built to solve a specific problem: easily generating a data dictionary from AEP exports.

The exported files can be large, and you will typically have many. I chose NDJSON over Parquet for ease of use, as Parquet's nested format is difficult to work with.

To begin, export at least half a full working day's worth of data—this alone will generate a rich and useful data dictionary depending on your data volumes,

**Instructions**

**Prerequisites**

- Some means of exporting data, eg sFTP, Azure Blob Storage
- Python installed on your machine, I use <https://www.python.org/> and run it on the command line.
- A Production or UAT Sandbox with data flowing into it, typically via SDK/alloy.js
- A Z: on the local filesystem.
  - If not, change file paths in the script.

**Copy the folder from my GitHub to your Z:**

Literally just copy/paste the files onto your file system and run it

Assuming it works (it should just go), you will now have an AEP Health Dashboard based on Luma Test Data!

**Running makedict.py with your org’s data:**

1. In AEP, go to **Connections > Destinations**.
2. Choose a destination (e.g., Secure FTP or Azure Blob Storage).

![](data:image/png;base64,)  

1. Configure the export format:  
    - File Type: JSON
    - Compression: .gz

![](data:image/png;base64,)  

1. Set the export to run for 1–14 days depending on data volume.

![](data:image/png;base64,)

1. Wait
2. Once exported, the files will be visible in your client:
3. ![](data:image/png;base64,)
4. You're now ready to run the dashboard for your org and generate your first data dictionary - whoop whoop!
5. Pull the files into Z:/input
6. Run the script
7. The output will be called .csv.
